subject: Civic Education
competence: Develops leadership qualities, identifying the need of leadership
lesson: Names the democratic leadership qualities in leadership: School Prefect Board Tribunal: Investigating Leadership Needs
unique_learning_outcome: Names the democratic leadership qualities in leadership.
Explains the need of moral leadership for the wellbeing of society.
the_entrance: 5-minute introduction: The teacher greets the 35 students divided into 7 groups and poses a relatable Sri Lankan school dilemma: 'Imagine our school sports meet is coming up, and the prefect board is divided on how to manage the entrance gates. One prefect wants to give orders strictly without listening, while another wants to consult all class monitors.' The teacher asks the class to consider which approach builds a peaceful school environment, seamlessly launching the School Prefect Board Tribunal activity.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher circulates among the seven groups, distributing mini-case study task sheets that outline daily challenges faced by a Sri Lankan school prefect board. The teacher facilitates group role allocation (Leader, Scribe, Timekeeper, Spokesperson, Civic Investigator) and prompts students to read the cases to uncover initial definitions of leadership.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Students organize themselves into their 7 assigned teams of 5, formally assign their group roles, and read through the prefect board case briefs. The Scribe records the team's initial brainstorming ideas regarding what leadership means in a school setting.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Mini-case study task sheets, student notebooks, colored markers

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: Acting as a facilitator, the teacher moves between groups to probe student thinking with guiding questions such as, 'What happens when a prefect lacks moral grounding?' and 'Which of these behaviors reflect tolerance and listening?' The teacher scaffolds teams in analyzing democratic versus autocratic traits.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Team members actively debate the case scenarios, using their textbooks to extract specific democratic leadership qualities such as listening, equity, and honesty. The Civic Investigator checks textbook facts while the Scribe drafts the group's arguments on chart paper.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Chart paper, marker pens, textbook excerpts on democratic leadership qualities

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher moderates the brief presentations from group spokespersons, inviting peer feedback and drawing out core concepts on the chalkboard. The teacher synthesizes how moral leadership directly ensures institutional wellbeing and societal harmony.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Group Spokespersons present their 3-part comparison charts detailing the definition of leadership, democratic qualities, and reasons for moral leadership. Peer students evaluate the presentations, offering constructive feedback and recording key insights in their notebooks.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Completed chart paper posters, chalkboard, white chalk

summary: In a 2-minute synthesis, the teacher reviews student discoveries, emphasizing that leadership is guiding a group toward common goals, democratic qualities like listening and equity prevent conflicts, and moral leadership is vital for maintaining a peaceful and well-governed school community.
assessment_and_feedback_whole_lesson: Formative assessment is conducted through observation of group collaboration, evaluation of the 3-part comparison charts for accuracy regarding democratic qualities, and assessing the quality of peer feedback during presentations.
post_activity: 5-minute in-class assignment: Each student writes down one key democratic leadership quality and one reason why moral leadership matters on a slip of paper and drops it into the team collection box as an active in-class exit check.
selected_activity:
Activity: School Prefect Board Tribunal: Investigating Leadership Needs
Approach: Students examine the daily challenges of a Sri Lankan school prefect board to explore what leadership means and why moral leadership creates a peaceful school environment.
Student task: Students audit three mini-case studies on school leadership issues, extracting definitions of leadership, identifying democratic practices (consensus over authority), and arguing the necessity of moral leadership for institutional wellbeing.
Teacher facilitation: The teacher manages time across the 30-minute block, guiding student inquirers with targeted questions such as 'What happens when a leader lacks moral grounding?' and 'How do we define leadership based on this case?'
Expected output: A 3-part comparison chart detailing: 1) Definition of leadership, 2) Democratic qualities, and 3) Reasons why moral leadership ensures societal wellbeing.
Grouping: 7 teams (7 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer. All 35 students participate actively across the 7 table islands.
